terms.comment: Morgan–Owens’s phrase. Fōrmula alone is the pharmacists’ word for a recipe in the nineteenth-century books Morgan–Owens cites; culīnārius, of the kitchen, is in Lewis & Short (Fronto).

phrases.latin: Ita faciāmus ut praecipitur: duo ōva, nōn tria.
phrases.english: Let’s do as the recipe says: two eggs, not three.

phrases.latin: quod sī nōn ita, ut praecēpimus, permiscueris, subsīdent arōmata et adūrentur
phrases.english: but if you don’t stir it as we have told you, the spices will sink and burn

sources: Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. recipe.
Lewis & Short: formula · Lewis & Short: culinarius · Lewis & Short: praeceptum · Lewis & Short: praecipio
